hunks.baseline: It felt like sitting on a bed of thorns—or rather, walking a thorny path.
hunks.sol: It felt like sitting on a bed of thorns—or rather, walking down a path covered in them.

hunks.baseline: Every time I moved alongside Mae Jonghak, the countless gazes flying my way made my face prickle.
hunks.sol: As I walked beside Mae Jonghak, the countless gazes coming my way made my face prickle.

hunks.baseline: Those gazes were filled with awe and curiosity.
hunks.sol: They were filled with awe and curiosity.

hunks.baseline: Everyone knew now. The young martial artist who had been treated as nothing more than a lucky country bumpkin just days ago was, in fact, a great martial artist known as the Sword Saint.
hunks.sol: Everyone knew now. The young martial artist who had been dismissed as a lucky country bumpkin just days ago was actually the great martial artist known as the Sword Saint.

hunks.baseline: “Is that really him? Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
hunks.sol: “Is that really him? Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint?”

hunks.baseline: The people’s hushed conversations pierced my ears.
hunks.sol: Their hushed conversations slipped straight into my ears.

hunks.baseline: “But who’s the guy next to him?”
hunks.sol: “But who’s that next to him?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. I heard from someone yesterday that he grabbed Great Hero Mae Jonghak by the neck and talked to him like he was some punk, and—well, you know?”
hunks.sol: “That’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. I heard yesterday that he grabbed Great Hero Mae Jonghak by the neck and called him every name under the sun, and—well, you know?”

hunks.baseline: Fuck. Did I do that on purpose? I didn’t. I just didn’t know.
hunks.sol: Fuck. It wasn’t like I’d done it knowingly. I hadn’t known who he was.

hunks.baseline: When I glared at the whispering people, Mae Jonghak burst out laughing.
hunks.sol: When I glared at the whispering crowd, Mae Jonghak burst out laughing.

hunks.baseline: “It’s all right. Friends can act that way with each other. No need to worry.”
hunks.sol: “It’s all right. Friends can act that way with each other.”

hunks.baseline: We moved to a quiet rear garden, away from the crowd.
hunks.sol: We moved to a quiet rear garden away from the crowd.

hunks.baseline: It was still early spring, but the weather was warm and the flowers were in full bloom. Mae Jonghak walked while gazing at flowers whose names I didn’t know, then opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: It was still early spring, but the weather was warm and the flowers were in full bloom. Mae Jonghak gazed at blossoms whose names I didn’t know as we walked, then spoke.

hunks.baseline: “I heard you gave Cheongpung a great deal of help.”
hunks.sol: “I heard you were a great help to Cheongpung.”

hunks.baseline: “It was nothing worth calling help.”
hunks.sol: “I wouldn’t exactly call it help.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know the details, but if he went so far as to call you his Benefactor, he must have received considerable assistance.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know the details, but if he went so far as to call you his Benefactor, you must have done a great deal for him.”

hunks.baseline: He didn’t know the details. He really didn’t know them at all.
hunks.sol: He didn’t know the details. He really, really didn’t.

hunks.baseline: I wondered what expression would cross Mae Jonghak’s face if he found out that I had merely given Cheongpung a few candied hawthorn skewers[^1] and earned the title of Benefactor.
hunks.sol: I almost wanted to see the look on Mae Jonghak’s face if he learned that a few candied hawthorn skewers[^1] were all it had taken for Cheongpung to start calling me his Benefactor.

hunks.baseline: “To be honest, I was very worried about that boy. But after meeting you this time, I was able to put my mind at ease. I owe you a debt.”
hunks.sol: “To be honest, I’d been very worried about that boy. But after meeting you, I was able to put my mind at ease. I owe you a debt.”

hunks.baseline: I decided not to mention the candied hawthorn skewers. There was no reason to cut into my own flesh when the Sword Saint said he owed me a debt.
hunks.sol: I decided not to mention the candied hawthorn skewers. If the Sword Saint said he owed me a debt, there was no reason to sell myself short.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, dear. And what happened?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, dear. What happened?”

hunks.baseline: “Hmm? He quieted down when I gave him dumplings.”
hunks.sol: “Hmm? He quieted down when I gave him some dumplings.”

hunks.baseline: I had a hard time forcing the words out.
hunks.sol: I struggled to force the words out.

hunks.baseline: “Is there a possibility that he might never wake up…?”
hunks.sol: “Is there a chance he might never wake up…?”

hunks.baseline: Remembering the old physician who had briefly visited yesterday and looked like a mouse, my mood soured.
hunks.sol: Remembering the mouse-faced old physician who had briefly visited yesterday instantly soured my mood.

hunks.baseline: “A quack? You mean the Luoyang Strange Physician?”
hunks.sol: “A quack? The Luoyang Strange Physician?”

hunks.baseline: “The Luoyang Strange Physician or whatever. He took a quick look, said there was nothing he could do for him right now, and stormed out. How is that not quackery?”
hunks.sol: “The Luoyang Strange Physician or whatever. He took one quick look, said there was nothing he could do right now, and walked straight out. How is that not quackery?”

hunks.baseline: What kind of old man had such a fierce temper? When I grabbed his arm in sheer disbelief, he screamed so loudly my ears nearly fell off.
hunks.sol: What kind of old man had such a vicious temper? When I grabbed his arm in disbelief, he shrieked loudly enough to burst my eardrums.

hunks.baseline: He shouted that he would never examine Jeok Cheongang again, leaving me no choice but to let him go.
hunks.sol: Then he shouted that he would never examine Jeok Cheongang again, leaving me no choice but to let him go.

hunks.baseline: “The Luoyang Strange Physician is a renowned doctor throughout the Central Plains. His personality is as eccentric as his nickname suggests, but there is no question about his skill.”
hunks.sol: “The Luoyang Strange Physician is renowned throughout the Central Plains. His temperament is every bit as eccentric as his epithet suggests, but his skill is beyond question.”

hunks.baseline: My heart sank when Mae Jonghak nodded.
hunks.sol: My heart sank at Mae Jonghak’s nod.

hunks.baseline: My thoughts must have shown plainly on my face, because he patted me on the back.
hunks.sol: It must have shown plainly on my face, because he gave me a few reassuring pats on the back.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang had seemed like he would shake everything off and get back on his feet in no time.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang had seemed like he would shake it off and get back on his feet in no time.

hunks.baseline: For the past year, he had been my Master, freely passing everything he had on to me. At the same time, he was as good as my own grandfather.
hunks.sol: For the past year, he had been my Master, passing everything he had on to me without reservation. At the same time, he was as good as my own grandfather.

hunks.baseline: A martial artist counted among the top ten in the world and a renowned physician had already examined Jeok Cheongang. For now, the best I could do was trust them.
hunks.sol: A martial artist counted among the ten greatest in the world and a renowned physician had already examined Jeok Cheongang. For now, all I could do was trust them.

hunks.baseline: When I finished thinking, I changed the subject.
hunks.sol: Having settled on that, I changed the subject.

hunks.baseline: Mae Jonghak gazed at the flower garden with a strange expression.
hunks.sol: Mae Jonghak gazed at the flower garden with an odd expression.

hunks.baseline: “What parts are you talking about?”
hunks.sol: “Which parts?”

hunks.baseline: “Let me ask you something. Did you notice anything strange about this incident?”
hunks.sol: “Let me ask you something. Did anything about this incident strike you as strange?”

hunks.baseline: I thought deeply for a moment before answering.
hunks.sol: I thought for a while before answering.

hunks.baseline: So much had happened so urgently yesterday that I hadn’t noticed it at the time, but there were certainly several things that raised questions.
hunks.sol: Too much had happened too quickly yesterday for me to notice at the time, but there were definitely several things that didn’t add up.

hunks.baseline: “There are a few things that seemed strange to me…”
hunks.sol: “There were a few things that seemed strange…”

hunks.baseline: “What are they?”
hunks.sol: “Such as?”

hunks.baseline: The leaders of the orthodox faction’s Murim had all gathered in one place.
hunks.sol: The leaders of the orthodox Murim had all gathered in one place.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: If Dark Heaven’s goal was to destroy the orthodox faction and take control of the world, they should have at least planted explosives.
hunks.sol: If Dark Heaven’s goal was to destroy the orthodox faction and seize control of the world, they could at least have tried planting explosives.

hunks.baseline: Whether or not it would have succeeded, it was a perfect opportunity to wipe out the enemy’s leadership all at once.
hunks.sol: Whether it succeeded or not, it was a golden opportunity to wipe out the enemy’s leadership in one stroke.

hunks.baseline: “Yet only Dharma King Hong Dao and Shaolin Temple had paid the price. They chose clear targets and acted from the very beginning.”
hunks.sol: “Yet the only ones sacrificed were Dharma King Hong Dao and Shaolin Temple. Those bastards chose specific targets from the beginning and acted accordingly.”

hunks.baseline: “Coming out into the open like this means they must have made at least some preparations for a fight… Yet it feels like they openly revealed themselves only to pick up iron coins instead of silver nyang.”
hunks.sol: “Revealing themselves like this means they must have made at least some preparations for war… But it feels like they exposed themselves in broad daylight just to take a few iron coins instead of the silver nyang.”

hunks.baseline: “That comparison is wrong. Shaolin Temple is a symbol of the orthodox faction. Dark Heaven destroyed that symbol to make their existence known.”
hunks.sol: “That comparison is wrong. Shaolin Temple is a symbol of the orthodox faction. By destroying that symbol, Dark Heaven made sure the world knew they existed.”

hunks.baseline: “Several theories have emerged. The first is that they wanted a direct confrontation.”
hunks.sol: “Several theories have emerged. The first is that they want a direct confrontation.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t underestimate demonic practitioners. They are people ruled solely by blood and power. The Demonic Cult during the Great Faction War was no different. They’re impossible to read.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t underestimate demonic practitioners. They are ruled by nothing but blood and power. The Demonic Cult was no different during the Great Faction War. They’re impossible to predict.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. They were great demonic figures who made their names feared beneath the Demonic Cult’s banner during the Great Faction War. A great deal of time has passed, but there’s still a strong possibility that they continue to follow the Demonic Cult.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. They were great fiends who earned fearsome reputations beneath the Demonic Cult’s banner during the Great Faction War. Many years have passed, but there’s still a strong possibility that they remain followers of the Demonic Cult.”

hunks.baseline: So Dark Heaven could be a franchise of the Demonic Cult. No, a subordinate organization.
hunks.sol: So Dark Heaven might be a Demonic Cult franchise. No, a subordinate organization.

hunks.baseline: As Mae Jonghak said, it was a possibility that made perfect sense.
hunks.sol: As Mae Jonghak said, it was entirely possible.

hunks.baseline: But there was one thing that bothered me…
hunks.sol: But there was still one thing bothering me.

hunks.baseline: “What about the Blood Lord? Is he part of the Demonic Cult, too?”
hunks.sol: “What about the Blood Lord? Is he part of the Demonic Cult too?”

hunks.baseline: “The Temporary Strength Pill you acquired, the Exploding Blood Demonic Art used by those who attacked Shaolin, and the Blood Lord himself. They all clearly carry the scent of the Demonic Cult, but… something is different. It has become darker and stranger.”
hunks.sol: “The Temporary Strength Pill you acquired, the Exploding Blood Demonic Art used by the attackers at Shaolin, and the Blood Lord himself. They all clearly carry the scent of the Demonic Cult, but… something is different. It’s darker and stranger.”

hunks.baseline: Mae Jonghak was a living witness to the Great Faction War, having lived through it himself. He must have fought countless enemies and experienced their martial arts firsthand.
hunks.sol: Mae Jonghak was a living witness to the Great Faction War. He must have fought countless enemies and experienced their martial arts firsthand.

hunks.baseline: In the orthodox Murim, he was one of the foremost authorities on demonic martial arts. His word was practically the established theory of the field.
hunks.sol: He was one of the orthodox Murim’s foremost authorities on demonic martial arts. Anything he said might as well have been academic consensus.

hunks.baseline: “Especially that sorcery I saw at the end. Even I had never experienced anything like it.”
hunks.sol: “Especially that sorcery I witnessed at the end. Even I had never encountered anything like it.”

hunks.baseline: I had heard that the Demonic Cult possessed all sorts of bizarre sorceries, but I never imagined something like that was possible.
hunks.sol: I had heard that the Demonic Cult possessed all sorts of bizarre sorceries, but I had never imagined anything like that was possible.

hunks.baseline: Even I, who was used to magic, had been left gaping in astonishment.
hunks.sol: Even I, someone accustomed to magic, had been left gaping in astonishment.

hunks.baseline: Martial artists had searched the surrounding area thoroughly, keeping every possibility in mind, but the Blood Lord was nowhere to be found. He had truly vanished as though the earth itself had swallowed him.
hunks.sol: Martial artists had scoured the surrounding area in case he was still nearby, but the Blood Lord was nowhere to be found. He had truly vanished as though the earth had swallowed him.

hunks.baseline: “There has also been considerable debate over where such a large number of enemies appeared from. If they can use that kind of sorcery on a large scale…”
hunks.sol: “There has also been considerable debate over where so many enemies came from. If they can use that kind of sorcery on a large scale…”

hunks.baseline: Calling it a surprise attack was laughable. If the enemies could appear here and there like Hong Gil-dong, it would be no different from being struck by lightning.
hunks.sol: Calling it a surprise attack wouldn’t even begin to cover it. If the enemy could pop up east and west like Hong Gil-dong, it would be like a bolt from the blue every time.

hunks.baseline: *The leadership must be in chaos, too.*
hunks.sol: *The leadership must be in chaos too.*

hunks.baseline: “They could have just broken it.”
hunks.sol: “They could have simply broken it.”

hunks.baseline: “I think they were more focused on taking it. To be honest, I’m not even sure what they planned to do with it.”
hunks.sol: “I think they were more interested in taking it. Honestly, I’m not even sure what they planned to do with it.”

hunks.baseline: As far as I knew, the Green Jade Buddha Staff was nothing more than a slightly special staff.
hunks.sol: As far as I knew, the Green Jade Buddha Staff was nothing more than a slightly unusual staff.

hunks.baseline: I thought it only seemed more impressive because it carried the authority of Shaolin’s Abbot and the history of a thousand-year-old Shaolin Temple.
hunks.sol: I figured it only seemed impressive because it embodied the authority of Shaolin’s Abbot and a thousand years of Shaolin history.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t the Elder Wand or anything. What were they going to do with a glowing green staff?
hunks.sol: It wasn’t the Elder Wand or anything. What were they going to do with a fluorescent green staff?

hunks.baseline: “Yes, that’s possible. That was what the others thought as well.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, that may be so. The others thought the same.”

hunks.baseline: After saying that, Mae Jonghak fell into thought for a while before suddenly speaking again.
hunks.sol: Mae Jonghak fell into thought for a while, then abruptly spoke again.

hunks.baseline: “Perhaps he sensed his own fate and left some arrangements behind. In the letter, he wrote that you were the Morning Star who would drive away the darkness.”
hunks.sol: “Perhaps he sensed his own fate and made preparations. In the letter, he wrote that you were the Morning Star who would drive away the darkness.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re a genius unlike anyone I’ve ever seen. Look around you. Who else your age has reached such a realm?”
hunks.sol: “You’re a genius unlike any I’ve ever seen. Look around you. Who else your age has reached such a realm?”

hunks.baseline: “Oh. I see.”
hunks.sol: “Oh. Right.”

hunks.baseline: “Pung broke through the wall to the Peak realm when he was eighteen. I’d have thought you had done about the same by that age.”
hunks.sol: “Pung broke through the wall to the Peak realm when he was eighteen. I’d have thought you were about the same at that age.”

hunks.baseline: “I was doing well in another sense back then. My epithet was the Night King.”
hunks.sol: “I was doing well in a different sense back then. My epithet was the Night King.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, something about being a match for the Ten Kings? Is that what it means?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, did it mean you were comparable to the Ten Kings?”

hunks.baseline: Mae Jonghak scratched the back of his head, unable to find anything to say, then let out a hollow laugh.
hunks.sol: Mae Jonghak scratched the back of his head, momentarily unable to find anything to say, then let out a hollow laugh.

hunks.baseline: “As expected of my grandson.”
hunks.sol: “That’s my grandson.”

hunks.baseline: As I turned away, Mae Jonghak shouted behind me.
hunks.sol: As I turned away, Mae Jonghak shouted after me.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll drop by again soon! I’ll bring news that will surprise you, too!”
hunks.sol: “I’ll drop by again soon! And I’ll bring news that will surprise you!”

hunks.baseline: When I returned to the room where Jeok Cheongang lay, Hyuk Mujin bowed and greeted me. Unlike before, he looked thoroughly disciplined, and I smiled with satisfaction.
hunks.sol: When I returned to the room where Jeok Cheongang lay, Hyuk Mujin greeted me with a bow. Unlike before, he now stood rigidly at attention, and I smiled with satisfaction.

hunks.baseline: “That’s how you stand watch. You can draw your sword at any moment. What could be better?”
hunks.sol: “That’s how you stand guard. You can draw your sword at any moment. Isn’t that nice?”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. I will guard this place like an iron fortress.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. I’ll guard this place like an iron fortress.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin was about to hurry out of the room when I spoke.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin was about to dart out of the room when I spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Put the gold lump in your sleeve back down.”
hunks.sol: “Put the lump of gold in your sleeve back down.”

hunks.baseline: “If it isn’t down by the time I count to three, you’ll be killed today. One, two.”
hunks.sol: “If it isn’t down by the time I count to three, you’re getting murdered today. One, two.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin put down the gold mask he had crumpled with his strength earlier and lowered his head dejectedly.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin put down the gold mask I had crushed into a lump earlier and lowered his head dejectedly.

hunks.baseline: “Captain, please. I even took out a loan from Yama himself this time…[^2]”
hunks.sol: “Captain, please. I even took on Yama’s Debt this time…[^2]”

hunks.baseline: I clicked my tongue and tucked the gold lump into my robes.
hunks.sol: I clicked my tongue and tucked the lump of gold into my robes.

hunks.baseline: “We’ll see, depending on how you behave.”
hunks.sol: “We’ll see. It depends on how you behave.”

hunks.baseline: I looked out the window. The sky was gradually turning red.
hunks.sol: I looked out the window. The sky was slowly turning red.

hunks.baseline: “The deadline is tomorrow morning. Can you do it?”
hunks.sol: “Until tomorrow morning. Can you manage that?”

hunks.baseline: “I will give my life.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll give my life.”

hunks.baseline: “I know you’re not going to do that anyway, so just do what I told you.”
hunks.sol: “I already know you won’t, so just do what I told you.”

hunks.baseline: I gazed at Jeok Cheongang’s face, which looked as though he were sleeping soundly, then lay down on the bed beside him.
hunks.sol: I gazed at Jeok Cheongang’s face as he slept soundly, then lay down on the bed beside him.

hunks.baseline: *How long had it been since I’d done this?*
hunks.sol: *How long had it been?*

hunks.baseline: The past year had been a nonstop rush. Now, I desperately wanted to ease off the reins a little and return to my family’s embrace.
hunks.sol: I had spent the past year running without a moment’s rest. Now, I desperately wanted to loosen the reins a little and return to my family’s embrace.

hunks.baseline: Ding.
hunks.sol: *Ding.*

hunks.sol: [^2]: “Yama’s Debt” is Taekyung’s joking term for a ruinous loan or loan-shark debt.
